items.title: Bifurcation, Loss of Hyderabad & the New Capital Amaravati
items.body:
## The bifurcation shock

- Under the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 (Act 6 of 2014)** — assent **1 March 2014**, appointed day **2 June 2014** — **Telangana** (10 districts, including **Hyderabad**) was carved out.
- Assets and liabilities were divided mainly on the **population ratio 58.32 : 41.68** (AP : Telangana).
- **Hyderabad**, the largest revenue and IT/services engine of the united state, went to Telangana; it stayed the **common capital for a maximum of 10 years** (Sec 5).
- Residuary AP thus lost a mature revenue base **and** had no ready capital — the twin cause of its post-2014 fiscal stress.

## Amaravati — greenfield capital

- **Amaravati**, on the **right bank of the Krishna** in Guntur district (near Vijayawada), was chosen as the new greenfield capital (founded 2014).
- Built on land assembled through a **Land Pooling Scheme (LPS)** from farmers; capital area ~217 km², seed capital ~17 km².
- Governed by **APCRDA**; major capital works later drew **World Bank/AIIB** funding support.
keyPoints: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 (Act 6 of 2014): assent 1 Mar 2014, appointed day 2 Jun 2014; Telangana carved out.
Assets/liabilities split mainly on population ratio 58.32 : 41.68 (AP : Telangana).
Hyderabad went to Telangana but stayed common capital for a maximum of 10 years.
Amaravati is the greenfield capital on the Krishna's right bank in Guntur district, built via a Land Pooling Scheme.
Losing Hyderabad's revenue plus funding a new capital was the core post-bifurcation fiscal shock.
items.mnemonic: Appointed day = 2/6 (2 June) 2014; ratio 58.32:41.68 favours AP.

items.title: Macro Snapshot — GSDP, Growth, Per-capita & Sector Shares
items.body:
## Size and growth

- **GSDP (2026-27) ~₹19.75 lakh crore (~US$205 bn)** — AP ranks about **8th-9th** among Indian states.
- Recent **GSDP growth**: 6.19% (2023-24), **8.21% (2024-25)**, ~**9.88% (2025-26)** — frequently above the national rate (Q2 2025-26 ~11.28% vs ~8.7% national).
- **Per-capita income**: ~₹2.38 lakh (2023-24, current prices), rising to ~**₹2.98 lakh (nominal, 2024-25)**; per-capita rank ~15th (mid-table).

## Sectoral composition (GSVA, 2023-24)

| Sector | Share |
|---|---|
| Agriculture & allied | ~37% |
| Industry | ~23% |
| Services (tertiary) | ~40% |

- AP is **more agrarian than India** (national farm share ~18%) yet **services are its largest sector** — and their share is rising, marking a structural shift.

## Fiscal position

- **Public debt ~35% of GSDP** (2025-26 est.); persistent **revenue deficit** and fiscal deficit near the FRBM band — a legacy of lost Hyderabad revenues and capital spending.
keyPoints: GSDP 2026-27 ~₹19.75 lakh crore; national rank ~8th-9th.
GSDP growth: 6.19% (2023-24), 8.21% (2024-25), ~9.88% (2025-26) — often above national rate.
Per-capita income ~₹2.98 lakh nominal (2024-25); rank ~15th.
Sector shares 2023-24: agriculture ~37%, industry ~23%, services ~40%.
AP is more agrarian than India (national farm share ~18%) but services are its largest sector.
Public debt ~35% of GSDP (2025-26 est.) with a persistent revenue deficit.
items.source: MoSPI GSVA; AP Planning Dept; PRS AP Budget Analysis 2025-26 (verified Sep 2026)

items.title: Primary-sector Strength — Rice Bowl, Aquaculture & Horticulture
items.body:
## Agriculture — the rice bowl

- AP is the **"Rice Bowl of India"**; the **Krishna and Godavari deltas** anchor irrigated paddy, with the **Godavari, Krishna, Penna and Tungabhadra** as its main rivers.
- Agriculture and allied activities support roughly **60% of the population**, giving farm income outsized social weight even as its GVA share falls.

## Fisheries & aquaculture leadership

- AP is **India's leading aquaculture state**, producing the bulk of the country's **farmed shrimp** and a very large share of inland fish — a top foreign-exchange earner using the long coastline and delta backwaters.

## Horticulture leadership

- AP is a top producer of **chillies** (Guntur), **mangoes**, citrus and other fruits.
- Horticulture is **climate-resilient and higher-return per hectare**, driving a voluntary shift in the cropping pattern.
keyPoints: AP = 'Rice Bowl of India'; Krishna and Godavari deltas anchor paddy.
Four main rivers: Godavari, Krishna, Penna, Tungabhadra; ~60% of people depend on agriculture.
AP is India's leading aquaculture state — dominant in farmed shrimp and inland fish exports.
Horticulture leader: Guntur chillies, mangoes, citrus; climate-resilient and high-return.
Allied sectors (fisheries, horticulture) increasingly drive farm-sector value.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic data; fisheries & horticulture depts (verified Sep 2026)

items.title: Water Resources, River Boards & the Polavaram National Project
items.body:
## Krishna-Godavari disputes & boards

- The Act set up two boards under an **Apex Council** (chaired by the Union Water Resources Minister): the **Krishna River Management Board (HQ in AP)** and the **Godavari River Management Board (HQ in Telangana)**.
- Krishna and Godavari **water-sharing remain live AP-Telangana disputes**; the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal's term was extended for project-wise allocations.

## Polavaram — lifeline project

- The **Polavaram project on the Godavari** (Eluru district) was declared a **National Project** under **Section 90**, with the Centre responsible for its development (Telangana's consent deemed given).
- **Multipurpose**: irrigation of ~23 lakh acres, a **960 MW** hydel powerhouse (12 × 80 MW) and drinking water; reservoir gross storage ~194 tmcft.
- Engineering highlights: a deep **diaphragm wall** under the earth-cum-rockfill dam and a large river diversion; it remains under construction with completion targeted later this decade.
keyPoints: Krishna Board HQ in AP; Godavari Board HQ in Telangana; both under an Apex Council (Union Water Minister).
Polavaram is on the Godavari (Eluru district), declared a National Project under Sec 90 of the Act.
Multipurpose: ~23 lakh acres irrigation, 960 MW hydel (12 x 80 MW), drinking water; ~194 tmcft storage.
Centre executes Polavaram; Telangana's consent is deemed given under Sec 90.
Krishna-Godavari water-sharing is a continuing AP-Telangana dispute.
items.mnemonic: Boards swap intuitively: Krishna->AP, Godavari->Telangana (K before G, AP before TS alphabetically).
items.source: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 (Sec 84-90); Polavaram Project Authority/APGENCO (verified Sep 2026)

items.title: Industry, Ports, Visakhapatnam & the VCIC Corridor
items.body:
## Coastline and ports

- AP has **India's second-longest coastline (after Gujarat)** — ~974 km — with **Visakhapatnam** as its only **major (central) port**, plus non-major ports at **Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada and Machilipatnam**.

## Visakhapatnam — the economic hub

- **Vizag** is AP's largest city and its commercial, IT and financial hub (steel plant, port, IT SEZ at Rushikonda) and anchors the corridor's northern end.

## VCIC / East Coast Economic Corridor

- The **Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC)** is the first phase of the **East Coast Economic Corridor (ECEC)** — **India's first coastal economic corridor** — supported by the **ADB**.
- Key nodes: **Visakhapatnam, Machilipatnam, Donakonda** and the **Chittoor/Srikalahasti-Yerpedu** area; the Reorganisation Act itself directed examining a Vizag-Chennai corridor on DMIC lines.
keyPoints: AP has India's second-longest coastline (~974 km) after Gujarat; Visakhapatnam is its major port.
Non-major ports: Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada, Machilipatnam.
Visakhapatnam is AP's largest city and commercial/IT/financial hub.
VCIC is the first phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor — India's first coastal corridor, ADB-backed.
VCIC nodes: Visakhapatnam, Machilipatnam, Donakonda, Chittoor/Srikalahasti area.
items.source: AP Socio-Economic data; ADB VCIC/ECEC; AP Reorganisation Act 2014, 13th Schedule (verified Sep 2026)

items.title: Swarna Andhra Vision@2047, Regional Disparities, Districts & e-Governance
items.body:
## Swarna Andhra Vision@2047

- AP's **long-term development vision**, aligned with **Viksit Bharat@2047**, to make the state a developed, high-per-capita economy with sustained double-digit growth by 2047, framed on guiding principles and a **Public-Private-People (P4)** approach.

## Regional disparities

- Growth is uneven: **Coastal Andhra** (Krishna-Godavari deltas, Vizag) is relatively developed, while **Rayalaseema** (drought-prone) and **North Coastal Andhra / Uttarandhra** lag — the Act names these two for a **special development package** (Sec 46).

## Districts & governance

- **District reorganisation**: 13 -> **26 (4 Apr 2022)** -> **28 (from 31 Dec 2025)**, adding Polavaram and Markapuram.
- **MeeSeva** is AP's flagship integrated **e-governance** platform for time-bound online citizen services.

## The Special Category Status debate

- **SCS** was a **Rajya Sabha assurance (Feb 2014)**, not a statutory clause; the Centre later offered a **Special Package** in lieu — a continuing centre-state flashpoint.
keyPoints: Swarna Andhra Vision@2047 = AP's long-term developed-state vision aligned with Viksit Bharat, using a P4 (Public-Private-People) model.
Coastal Andhra is developed; Rayalaseema and North Coastal AP lag and are named for a special package (Sec 46).
Districts: 13 -> 26 (Apr 2022) -> 28 (from 31 Dec 2025, adding Polavaram & Markapuram).
MeeSeva is AP's flagship integrated e-governance citizen-service platform.
Special Category Status was a Rajya Sabha assurance, not in the Act; a Special Package was offered instead.
items.source: Government of AP (Swarna Andhra Vision@2047, e-governance); AP Reorganisation Act 2014 (verified Sep 2026)

items.title: AP infrastructure — transport, energy & ICT
items.body:
## Transport

- **Ports:** AP has India's **second-longest coastline (~975 km)**. Operational ports include the central-government **Visakhapatnam Port**, and non-major ports **Krishnapatnam** (Nellore), **Gangavaram** (Visakhapatnam; deep-water, ~21 m draft, now Adani-operated) and **Kakinada**. New greenfield ports under the **AP Maritime Board** are being built at **Ramayapatnam** (Prakasam), **Machilipatnam** (Krishna) and Kakinada.
- **Airports:** existing airports at **Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada (Gannavaram), Tirupati, Kurnool (Orvakal), Rajahmundry, Kadapa, Puttaparthi**. The greenfield **Bhogapuram International Airport** (Vizianagaram district), officially named **Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport**, is under construction off **NH-16** near Visakhapatnam.
- **Roads & rail:** **NH-16 (Chennai-Kolkata, Golden Quadrilateral)** is the arterial highway. A dedicated railway zone — **South Coast Railway (SCoR)** — was sanctioned with headquarters at **Visakhapatnam** (divisions: Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam).

## Energy

- Generation mix of thermal (**Dr NTTPS, Vijayawada**; Krishnapatnam), hydro and fast-growing **renewable energy** (solar & wind); AP is a leading solar/wind state and is developing large **pumped-storage** and **green-hydrogen** projects. **Polavaram** adds **960 MW** of hydel capacity.

## ICT / digital

- **AP State FiberNet (APSFL / AP FiberNet)** — a state-owned network (since 2015) providing broadband, IPTV and phone connectivity to homes and offices.
- **MeeSeva** single-window e-services and the **Real Time Governance Society (RTGS)** support digital service delivery. **Visakhapatnam** is promoted as the state's **IT / executive hub**, with IT investment along the **VCIC**.
keyPoints: Transport: ~975 km coastline (2nd longest); ports — Visakhapatnam (major), Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada; new Ramayapatnam & Machilipatnam.
Airports incl. greenfield Bhogapuram = Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport (Vizianagaram) off NH-16.
South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone HQ at Visakhapatnam; NH-16 is the arterial Golden-Quadrilateral highway.
Energy: thermal + hydro + fast-growing renewables (solar/wind), pumped-storage & green hydrogen; Polavaram adds 960 MW hydel.
ICT: AP FiberNet (APSFL, since 2015) broadband/IPTV; MeeSeva & RTGS digital services; Vizag as IT hub.
Infrastructure development spans transport, energy and ICT — central to AP’s growth.
items.source: AP Maritime Board; AAI/Bhogapuram (Alluri Sitarama Raju Intl Airport); South Coast Railway (Indian Railways); APSFL (AP FiberNet); APGENCO/APTRANSCO (verified Sep 2026)

items.title: AP flagship projects — Amaravati capital & Polavaram (status)
items.body:
## Amaravati — the greenfield capital

- Located in **Guntur district** on the **Krishna** river, ~15 km SW of Vijayawada, within the Vijayawada-Guntur-Tenali urban region.
- Built on land contributed by farmers under a **Land Pooling Scheme (LPS)**; planned by **APCRDA**. After a period of uncertainty (the 2019-24 'three-capitals' proposal), Amaravati was **reaffirmed as the sole capital** and construction/funding (including World Bank/ADB support) resumed from 2024.

## Polavaram — national irrigation project

- A **multipurpose National Project** on the **Godavari** in **Eluru/Polavaram district**; the Centre funds the irrigation component.
- Designed to irrigate ~**23 lakh acres**, generate **960 MW** hydel power and supply drinking water; a **Godavari-Krishna** link is part of the design.
- Construction (diaphragm wall, cofferdams) is **advanced but incomplete**, with a revised completion timeline; it is central to stabilising the delta.

## Why they matter

Both are **capital-intensive, state-defining infrastructure**: Amaravati anchors administration and urban growth; Polavaram anchors irrigation, power and water security.
keyPoints: Amaravati: greenfield capital in Guntur dist. on the Krishna; built via farmers’ Land Pooling Scheme, planned by APCRDA.
Reaffirmed as AP’s sole capital; construction/funding (World Bank/ADB) resumed from 2024 after the ‘three-capitals’ phase.
Polavaram: multipurpose National Project on the Godavari (Eluru/Polavaram dist.); Centre funds irrigation.
Polavaram design: ~23 lakh acres irrigation, 960 MW hydel, drinking water, Godavari-Krishna link; advanced but incomplete.
Both are state-defining infrastructure — Amaravati for administration/urban growth, Polavaram for water/power security.
